summary.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 36.2% YoY to INR138.46 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 12.02% on raw material and gas cost spikes.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue for FY26 reached INR482.95 crore, up 35.32% YoY, with EBITDA of INR71.03 crore (14.71% margin) and PAT of INR23.20 crore. Q4 EBITDA margin dropped to 12.02% from the 16-17% range management cited earlier, which management attributed to raw material, gas, freight and outsourced labour cost increases in March 2026. Management expects margins to recover toward 15-16% if the war-related cost disruption does not worsen, and guided Q1 FY27 revenue at a similar run rate to Q4. Capacity is about 72,000 MTPA with FY26 output of 52,620 MT, and the company plans about 7,800 MT of foundry addition in H1 FY27.

segments.name: Large castings (gearboxes, transmission cases, differential carriers)
segments.commentary: Management calls large castings the main driver of product mix improvement, citing fewer competitors (about 8-10 in India for tractor large castings) and higher value addition.

segments.name: LFC (lost foam casting) via Meeta Casting
segments.commentary: Contributes about 10-15% of revenue and about 20% of the order book; management targets 30% in three years. Margin is about 1-2% higher than conventional castings.

segments.name: Railways
segments.commentary: Not yet material; product development and qualification ongoing with three to four products developed. Initial contributions expected in FY27.

guidance_outlook: Medium-term revenue target of INR600 crore; management says 15% growth for the next two years gets there. Also cited 15% growth for the company against 6-8% expected from customers in FY27.
Margins expected to recover toward 15-16% (EBITDA) if no further war-related disruption; Q1 FY27 revenue expected similar to Q4 FY26.

FY27 capex of about INR25-30 crore, of which about INR35 crore is for the 7,800 MT foundry addition (the figures on the 7,800 MT project were given inconsistently in the call). FY28 LFC project of 2,400 MT, with about INR60-70 crore capex.
Long-term target of crossing 1 lakh MT capacity by FY28.
Target minimum EBITDA of 18-20% for planned US finishing operations, versus 14-15% in India.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity about 72,000 MTPA across Dera Bassi, Hoshiarpur, Mohali and Tahliwal. Utilisation about 73-74% (around 52,000 MT); management says 80-85% is achievable in FY27 if market holds.
FY27: about 7,800 MT green sand foundry addition, to be commissioned in H1 FY27, plus matching machining capacity. Capacity to reach about 80,000 MT.
FY28: about 2,400 MT of LFC capacity; capacity to cross 1 lakh MT. Management said LFC capacity mix would be about 70/30 to 65/35 (conventional/LFC) after this addition.
Greenfield LFC economics: 3,000 MT capacity at about INR75 crore versus INR120-150 crore for conventional, roughly 50% lower capex.
Hoshiarpur land acquired via ARC auction was withdrawn after litigation; refund received. Company is looking for fresh land in about two to three months for capacity beyond 1-2 years.
demand_pricing: Customers expect 6-8% growth in FY27 with H2 facing a high base; company expects about 15% from new products and projects.
Company says it gained share with almost all customers: market grew 16-17% while the company grew 34%.
Top three customers (M&M, Swaraj, TAFE, Escorts named) contribute about 50-55% of revenue.
Order book described as overbooked; Vishal's estimate of INR500-600 crore was affirmed as easily achievable, but no official figure was stated.

Raw material cost up about 4-6% in March; management says raw material is passed through with about a one-quarter lag, while freight pass-through is being negotiated (monthly for some customers, quarterly for others).

Exports started to South Korea (one lot shipped, another going); Europe being explored. US subsidiary (Omnia Engineering Inc., Delaware) acquired for $50,000 with up to $100,000 planned; not yet operational.

qa_highlights.question: What is installed capacity and maximum utilisation, and why have EBITDA margins fallen?
qa_highlights.answer: Installed capacity is 72,000 MT; utilisation about 73-74%, with 80-85% achievable this year. Margin fell to 12% because raw material prices rose sharply in March, aggravated by gas issues; recovery expected from next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins fall in Q4, and will they recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw material rose about 4-6%, and gas, outsourced labour, manpower and freight costs also rose in March. Management expects a reversion to 15-16% margins if war-related disruption does not worsen.

qa_highlights.question: Capex plan and funding for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex about INR25-30 crore, with about INR35 crore for the 7,800 MT project per management. FY28 LFC project of 2,400 MT needs about INR60-70 crore, funded by debt and equity; FY27 funded by debt only.

qa_highlights.question: Debt levels and leverage comfort?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt rose to about INR180 crore this year, with interest cost about INR22 crore. Management said net debt-to-equity will stay below 1 at all times; comfortable at about 0.65.

qa_highlights.question: What is the US entity's margin profile and plan?
qa_highlights.answer: The US entity is aimed at direct US customers; initial work would be manufacturing in India, with later possible acquisition or a US plant. Finishing-only US operations are expected to give 18-20% EBITDA margins versus 14-15% in India.

qa_highlights.question: What is the LFC share of revenue and order book, and what is the margin?
qa_highlights.answer: LFC is about 10-15% of revenue and about 20% of the order book. Margin is 1-2% higher than conventional castings. Customers added include KION India (domestic) and one in South Korea.

risks_watch: Q1 FY27 margin recovery depends on stabilisation of gas, crude-linked chemicals and diesel/freight costs; freight pass-through is still under negotiation.
Debt rose to about INR180 crore in FY26, with interest about INR22 crore; FY28 capex funding mix depends on equity raise plans that were not specified.
The 7,800 MT addition's capex figure was stated inconsistently (INR35 crore vs an earlier INR60-70 crore for the project); clarity needed.
Customer concentration: top three customers are about 50-55% of revenue.
Legacy components (about 60% of mix per management) carry lower margins; the new-component mix shift will determine margin trajectory.
US entity and export ramp-up are early-stage, with no revenue or timeline disclosed.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volumes, demand and the 1 lakh MT vision, but noticeably vague and hedged on margin recovery timing, cost pass-through and capex funding, repeatedly qualifying outcomes with "if there is no further disruption."
key_quotes: Production volumes for Q4 financial year '26 stood at 14,193 metric tons, taking the full year F '26 volume to 52,620 metric tons, the highest in any single financial year in the company's history
So, I mean, I don't see a very, very major impact of these cost pressures for a long term', short-term impact will be there, but not on long-term basis.
We do 100% machined castings. We don't give raw castings.
